overview.headline: Binary search by halving a sorted interval

keyPoints.point: Students learn that binary search operates on a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the interval in half.
keyPoints.quote: Search a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that if the search key is less than the middle item the interval narrows to the lower half and otherwise to the upper half.
keyPoints.quote: If the value of the search key is less than the item in the middle of the interval, narrow the interval to the lower half.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that binary search on an ordered linked list still needs linear traversals but performs only logarithmic comparisons.
keyPoints.quote: It makes O(n) traversals, as does linear search, but it only performs O(log n) comparisons.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the midpoint calculation can overflow when high and low are near the largest expressible integer and a safe alternative exists.
keyPoints.quote: This overflows if high and low are close to the largest expressible integer.
